caption:
TRAINING DAY⚔️
✨CROSS CHOP EDITION‼️
Ft: @91._leroy @xavierlewis_90 

Snow cleared up just enough to get in with the guys 🤝🏾
… Despite it being back now hahaha 

Part of making plays is making plans ✍🏾🔥

You’re not going to make game changing plays if your body has never been there before. Muscle memory is a real thing. More specifically it’s your autonomic nervous system taking over and moving your body in a specific way when it recognizes something (I graduated 3 years ago I may still know a lil sum sum mayne) 🕺🏾

In all seriousness it’s quite literally the definition of what you do in the dark will show in the light☀️

@91._leroy said it the best 🗣️

Store bank reps so you feel comfortable cashing out on game day💯

Set up your rush, find your rhythm, speed it up, then burn it into your nervous system🤞🏾

caption:
TRAINING DAY⚔️
FT UNCs finest 💪🏾: @91._leroy @danderson.__ @xavierlewis_90 @niccomag58 

@91._leroy said it right, “ gotta get through 1st & 2nd down before you get to 3rd down”💯

Got the guys out on some grass/turf working on run fundamentals 🥋

The coaching points are GROUND TO THE MAN, and how do we train this⁉️

With handwork 🙌🏾and eye discipline 👁️👄👁️

With a progression of ground to man hands to dislodge blockers. Followed by sinking eyes below hand to control and maintain a base. When your man is defeated your chin tucks in your armpit to put your eyes in your gap, maintaining your responsibility. Then to cap it off, a violent disengage to make a play on the ball once it declares💪🏾

A common error is either bending at the elbow before the strike and not watching your hands land! You feet will follow your hands after you delivers blow with your hips. Gots to make sure those guided missiles land‼️

Comment “Foxy” and dm for training details 🤞🏾

LIKE, FOLLOW, and SHARE @trulytomari for more tips and tricks. As always, let’s continue to build this community together 💪🏾

caption:
Well, here we go. I've been putting this off for a while now. This is so hard. Hanging up the jersey that helped form me for 4 years into the person and player I've always wanted to be. Leaving a place that has been my home, a court that has been my safe place, and a team that has defined the trajectory of this program forever. This is one of the hardest things we do as athletes - give EVERYTHING we have for 4 years only to have to say goodbye all too soon. 

But gosh, am I the luckiest girl in the world. No, I never won a national championship. No, I never made a sweet sixteen. I didn't earn 1000 accolades. But, what I was a part of at Carolina is something I will never ever forget.

Amidst endless change, disagreements, tears, laughter, big tests, long bus rides, heart wrenching losses, and historic wins, I was part of a program that, no matter what, loved above all else. A value that goes far beyond us and points straight to my Father in Heaven. We never once gave up on eachother or on this program. We made one another better. We made this place ours. And we made our best friends. These people became a part of me, and this place became a piece of my DNA. And because of this team and the love we committed to, I had the blessing of helping to build a legacy that I hope goes far beyond my 4 years wearing that jersey. 

To my teammates, you helped me become the best version of Maddy May. I will miss every single moment with you. Yes, even the morning lifts and the cold hotel showers😭You are the most incredible group of women I've ever met. And I love you all so deeply. 

To my coaches, thank you for everything. For taking a chance on me, for never giving up on me, for making me feel seen and heard, for challenging me, and for teaching me what true leadership looks like. You all are the heartbeat of this incredible place.

I said this time last year that I would leave this chapter behind without an ounce of regret. And here I am sitting, with not one singular ounce. Just a whole lot of gratitude🩵

Thank you Carolina Volleyball. I will forever be marked by you. And I will forever be a Tar Heel. 

#25🫶

caption:
Volleyball, thank you for giving that meek 8 year old little girl in the video a purpose and a voice. I know she would be so unbelievably proud of all that we’ve accomplished. I couldn’t be more grateful to have had the chance to play this sport for the past 13 years. This sport will forever hold a special place in my heart and I’ll never be able to express the amount of valuable lessons it has taught me that has shaped me into the person I am today.

Thank you God for giving me the gift of volleyball. To my family thank you for believing in me and being behind me 100% while I pursued my dreams of playing this sport at the highest level. Specifically, thank you to my parents for teaching me that through hard work and dedication, anything is possible. 
To all my teammates that I’ve had over the years, thank you. Thank you for giving me life long memories on and off the court. To all the coaches that have believed in me and given me valuable lessons and skills to better myself not only as a volleyball player but also a person, thank you. I will miss doing what I love most and competing with my best friends everyday but I will forever hold onto the memories that I’ve made while playing this amazing sport.

caption:
February 12, 1953 - October 1, 2025 

To know him, was to love him. My grandpa was my everything. He was my rock, my safe place, and the man who taught me love. He lived a life full of humility, strength, and kindness. He was stable, consistent, and caring. To put it plainly, he was everything I strive to be. 

After a two year fight with stage 4 bone cancer, my grandpa has laid peacefully to rest. It feels like part of my heart has been ripped away from me, and I will long for another day with him for the rest of my life. He was my confidant and my best friend. 

He leaves behind a legacy of good people. He raised a family through the good, bad, and ugly. He never wavered in his Faith, never lost his hope, and always put others first. He taught me how to be kind. He taught me how to find the joy in the smallest of moments, and to never take a second for granted. He showed me how to care for the people around me. He taught me how to know a love that’s true. 

To my guardian angel, I love you💛

caption:
Two years. how has it already been two years? It still feels like we just started dating yesterday. Doing life with you is the best part of mine, and I can’t wait for everything that’s still ahead of us. You know I don’t really believe in luck, but somehow, I still feel like the luckiest girl in the world. I’ve never known anyone so kind, so caring, so full of love.
Thank you for loving me in ways I didn’t even know I needed. Thank you for being my calm, my comfort, and my home. Getting to watch you do your thing especially when you’ve got the keyboard set up in the apartment and you’re playing for me and Astro is one of my favorite things. You’ll always be my favorite musician. And speaking of Astro… you’re the best cat dad she could’ve ever dreamed of (and you know she’s picky). We’re both so lucky to be loved by you. And thank you for being my biggest supporter and the loudest voice at meets. You’ll always be my own personal hype man. I love you here’s to the rest of our lives! Also Happy birthday me‼️ 21!

caption: Words can’t describe the love I have for you. You never failed to leave me or anyone else with a full heart. I know God exists because of the love that poured from you and the light that would shine through you when you were around. The wisdom, the kindness, the strength, and the passion you had for Jesus are traits I pray I can come close to having during my lifetime. You never missed game regardless if it was basketball, volleyball, or the game you looked so forward to every year, softball. I’m forever thankful that the Lord gave you the chance to see me live out my dream at Carolina because you were one person that never let me feel like that dream was too big to accomplish. I will never forget the smile you welcomed me with and the hug you left me with every time I saw you. You made everything more special, from a stolen base, to getting a good grade, or just a simple lunch together. You made every moment better. To know you was to love you, and if you knew Him, it was without a doubt an honor. I can officially say you have the best seat in the house to every ball game, every graduation, and every wedding to come. I know you’re smiling down on all of your boys and your girl.😉I will love you forever my sweet papa, and I will never forget your sweet voice saying “Hey my love!”😇🩵

caption:
Thankful for every bit of my 10+ year swim journey…If swim has taught me one thing through the years it’s that growth does not happen without failure, disappointment, and setbacks. Journeys are full of learning opportunities, memories, both good and bad times and much more…
-Not all journeys have to have positive endings, because the truth is it doesn’t matter how it ends, it’s about how you made the journey worth while and the things you accomplished within it. It’s about how you respond when things don’t go your way, getting up when you get knocked down, continuing to move forward when it doesn’t feel possible. That’s how character is built. At the end of the day it’s you vs. you.

caption:
What A Season🩵

A year marked by hard work, discipline, belief, and love. To many on the outside, this probably looks like any other college volleyball team who made it to the round of 32. No. 

To us... to me, this is a group of people who decided a year ago that where we were wasn't good enough. A group of people who learned, trouble shooted, and had the guts to try something new. People who knew it wouldn't be easy, but that if, through everything, we loved eachother, we could create something special. 

I see a group who would run through brick walls for the people beside them. There was not a time that we made a decision and didn't think about the ripple effect it may have. Coaches and teammates who left everything on that court for eachother. We were a family. A Team.

This was a team who had coaches that deeply cared for each of us. A team where we showed up for eachother in whatever way was needed. A group that sobbed when we realized our season had come to an end. Not because we had lost, but because we could compete with this group of people forever. 

I'm so grateful to have experienced a season like this in my time as a collegiate athlete. Where we redefined what is means to be a Tar Heel Volleyball player, and set the foundation for years to come.

To my coaches and teammates, thank you. Words will never be enough to express how much I love each of you 🤍 What we did this year... so special, and I'm so proud.

More than anything in this post I want to thank You, God. For giving me this gift of volleyball to pursue and enjoy. For speaking so clearly to a 15 year old girl and telling her that UNC was exactly where she needed to be. Gosh were You right. Thank you Jesus for Your constant faithfulness.

And now, I've got one more go at this thing. This time next year, I'm determined to have not an ounce of regret in my body. So senior year, here I come.

.
.
.

caption:
The easiest people to celebrate on national coaches day!!!
Paul was my very first gymnastics coach when I started at 5 years old. Throughout these great 13 years of knowing him, I have come to be so grateful for the wonderful influence he has had on my life!!! I remember having to write a little paper on who our hero was when I was in the fourth grade. I chose Paul as mine and I would do so time and time again. Without his amazing coaching and support, I wouldn’t be anywhere near where I am today and that is something I will never forget. I’m so lucky to have so many touching memories to look back on from my years in club gymnastics and can attribute most of those fond memories to my caring coach!!!
With that being said, I am so excited to start a new chapter with my amazing future coaches and cannot wait to begin to work with them in Chapel Hill!!!

caption:
NEWS: UNC quarterback Max Johnson tells ESPN that he’ll return to UNC and play the 2025 season. The UNC grad student QB suffered a broken right leg in the opener against Minnesota. “I have a lot of football left in me, and know I will be back out there next year,” he said.

Johnson is grateful to the medical team caring for him, as he’s still recovering in Minnesota. He’s looking forward to rooting on UNC. “I’ll be there every day supporting my teammates and helping out as much as I can. I appreciate all the love and support from the fans.”

Here’s Johnson’s full statement to ESPN: Here’s Johnson’s full statement: “These last eight days have been a serious grind and it has taken a lot to get to the other side and start the recovery process. I want to thank Dr Templeman and his team, the nurses and support staff at Hennepin County Medical Center who took amazing care of me. Thank you to UNC Head Coach Mack Brown, the coaching staff, and trainers who have encouraged and supported me. Thank you to family and friends who have prayed and supported me during this time and ultimately my Lord and Savior that pulled me though. It will be hard to sit on the sidelines, but I have a lot of football left in me and know I will be back out there next year. In the meantime, I’ll be there every day supporting my teammates and helping out as much as I can. I appreciate all the love and support from the fans – #GoHeels.”

caption:
Semester Recap…

with the semester starting out rough with having a shooting that left us in lockdown for over 5 hours in only the third week of class and having another scare just two weeks later there was a lot of fear and lots of uncertainty while going into the rest of the semester. When things started to pick back up again and everything was going steady for a few weeks i hurt my shoulder. This was limiting my gymnastics and what i was capable of doing and eventually we decided it would be best if i just focused on rehab bad strengthening my shoulder to get me back and ready for season to start. While this was very hard for me to not be able to train and just wanting to be back in it taught me a lot about myself and gave me more time to focus on my well being and my mental health. I adopted a cat and that was the best decision i’ve ever made. Also in this semester i was able to get so much closer to the person who brings out the best in me and makes me the happiest i’ve ever been. We have gone on so many adventures and picked each other up when the other wasn’t doing the best. Knowing that i always have Holland in my corner and knowing that no matter what i can talk to him about anything and everything has been everything i’ve ever wanted. Now with the semester coming to an end with my last final tomorrow im starting to appreciate the little things like the sunrises in the mornings all of the friends i’ve made and all of the little things that ive done to better myself. I cannot wait to make so many more memories. I can’t wait to get back and ready for season. I can’t wait for what next semester holds for me.

caption:
Before I announce where I have decided to commit, this post 100% deserves to be posted first…
So to my day 1, @addison.sternbeck 
We started this journey together when we were 4. We grew up being together every single day, I remember having conversations  of us talking about where we would play in college together one day. That was always our dream. Well I want to tell you today we made it! Even though you won’t be there with me, because injuries won your battle, I want to say every time I step on the field I play for you. Your dad was our coach for over 10 years of our lives and taught us everything about the game, he made it fun and not like a job. Playing together showed me how the game should be played with ENERGY and EFFORT like Coach D always said. To us softball is more than a game it’s the memory’s we cherish together and the fight we both went through for it. We both struggled with injuries and we both went through tough situations to get back to playing the game we love, softball is my life and was yours, even though you don’t play anymore, I still remember the times we had together on the field. God put us together on the field for a reason to help us grow and compete, to show us meaning and true friendship, as well as LOVE FOR THE GAME. Softball will forever be a game that I play for others including you to show how it makes a person the best of themselves. My love for softball is forever, so congratulations again to Asquared because we made it! Like we always dreamed of🫶🫶

That was the day i tore my achilles and the day that i got a new outlook on a lot of things. Now here i am 9 months out and i’m college and slowly getting my skills back and learning new skills to accommodate for landings and i am having the best time being a Tar Heel.  The last video was today. I finally landed my new bar dismount!!
